chapters.title: This meeting at a glance
chapters.narrative: Scale, tempo, geography: how many abstracts, when they dropped, and whose turf it is. Everything that follows builds on this screen.

chapters.title: Where the heat is, and how mature the evidence is
chapters.narrative: Cancer types and domains say what everyone is racing for; staging, evidence type and overall assessment say how solid the result is. Read them together before carrying any conclusion forward.

chapters.act: Act III · Who is taking the position
chapters.title: Who runs the studies, and who owns the assets
chapters.narrative: Sponsors say who runs the study; originators say who owns the drug — usually not the same party. Then the concentration of targets, drugs and mechanisms, plus the cancer type → target → drug pathways.

chapters.title: Where China-based work stands at this meeting
chapters.narrative: China-related work defined by one hard rule — the sponsor is registered in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan: who leads, where it concentrates, and how its positivity rate compares with the rest of the world.

chapters.title: The few items that could change a decision
chapters.narrative: Compressing a thousand average data points into one page: why each item deserves action, and how far it can support a decision. No charts here — only the graded list.

chapters.title: Where it broke, where nobody goes, and what to watch
chapters.narrative: Where negative and terminated results cluster, which questions remain unanswered, and which assets and dates to watch over the next 6–12 months.

views.title: Where the sponsors are based
views.requirement: By the country or region where the sponsor is registered.

views.title: Most disclosed cancer types
views.requirement: Abstracts mentioning the cancer type; one abstract can count for several types, so shares sum to more than 100%.

views.title: Disease domains
views.requirement: By platform disease-domain tags; one abstract can belong to several domains.

views.title: Stage and setting
views.requirement: Platform stage tags, mixing trial phase (I/II/III) with disease setting (early, locally advanced, advanced). Abstracts without the tag are excluded.

views.title: Evidence types
views.requirement: By platform evidence-source tags: prospective or retrospective studies, real-world studies and trial phases each count separately.

views.title: Overall assessment
views.requirement: By platform result-assessment tags; unlabelled abstracts are shown as not assessed rather than counted as positive or unfavorable.

views.title: Stage by assessment
views.requirement: Abstracts per cross combination; empty cells are drawn as blank and mean no such study at this meeting.

views.title: Therapeutic area by stage
views.requirement: Abstracts per cross combination, limited to the six largest areas; blank cells mean no such study this year. Read early-phase brightness as how far forward a field's pipeline sits.

views.title: Evidence type by assessment
views.requirement: Abstracts per cross combination. The positive cell is visibly darker for real-world and retrospective rows — the most telling structural difference this year: looser designs are less often judged positive.

views.title: Leading sponsors
views.requirement: Counted per sponsor; multi-sponsor studies count once per sponsor, investigator-initiated and registrational studies alike.

views.title: Leading drug originators
views.requirement: Counted per drug originator/holder — a different lens from sponsors above: the sponsor may be a hospital or CRO while the drug belongs to someone else. The field records the **current holder** of the drug, so backbone chemotherapies (carboplatin, paclitaxel, gemcitabine, oxaliplatin) are held by generic manufacturers and inflate their rank; read this together with the drug ranking when judging the innovative portfolio.

views.title: Originators most studied by external sponsors
views.requirement: Only studies whose sponsors do not include the drug originator: mostly academic, hospital or partner-led validation rather than originator-run registrational work. The same current-holder caveat applies, so generic holders of backbone chemotherapies cluster near the top.

views.title: Most studied targets
views.requirement: Abstracts mentioning the target; each target in a combination counts separately.

views.title: Most disclosed drugs
views.requirement: Abstracts per drug; a multi-arm abstract counts once per drug, and each drug in a combination counts separately.

views.title: Mechanisms of action
views.requirement: By platform mechanism-of-action tags; a drug may carry several.

views.title: Cancer type → target → drug
views.requirement: Only the most disclosed cancer types with their targets and drugs, to read the pathways rather than the full distribution.

views.title: Cancer type × China-held / rest of world
views.requirement: Abstracts per cancer type for China-held drugs versus the rest of the world. China here means the drug development-institute region includes mainland China / Hong Kong / Macau / Taiwan, which also captures imported drugs held by a China entity of a multinational; overlap with the China-sponsor lens is partial (see the next chart).

views.title: How the two China lenses overlap
views.requirement: Cross-tab of China-held drugs (drug research-institute region includes mainland China / Hong Kong / Macau / Taiwan) against China-based sponsors. Only studies hitting at least one lens are shown. Asset-only entries are mostly imported drugs held by a China entity of a multinational; sponsor-only entries are mostly local studies run on foreign-owned assets.

views.title: Targets China-held drugs concentrate on
views.requirement: Target ranking within China-related work; compare with the overall ranking to see whether it follows the global mainstream or runs on its own track.

views.title: China-based sponsors
views.requirement: This chart uses the research-side lens: sponsors registered in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan, with China subsidiaries of multinationals counted where registered. Read it alongside the asset-side charts above — who does the work and who holds the drug are two different questions.

views.title: Where negative and terminated results cluster
views.requirement: Only studies assessed as negative or terminated; this is the denominator for where things broke, excluding unassessed work.
